title: New data show the object separated from the seabed
summary: Dennis Asberg tells of New data show the object separated from the seabed, about June 2025 at Baltic Sea anomaly, between Sweden and Finland, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: It looks like it's separated from the bottom. That's what I can say.

plain: A Swedish treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg, whose team found a strange shape on the floor of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland, says new data from June 2025 show the object sits apart from the seabed. "That's what I can say," he says. If so, it would mean the object is not just part of the sea floor.
